input.subject: Monkey D. Luffy
input.continuity: One Piece manga through the end of Wano Country arc
input.intent: Perform a PRICE-ONLY balance refinement of this newly generated same-campaign Luffy via the standard pipeline. Double base cost from700 to1400 and double EACH of the15 purchase costs exactly. Preserve every other field EXACTLY: all descriptions (including corrected contactStun eligibility), stats, form/Technique names and numbers, IDs, Haki paths, shared unlock tiers, resources and mechanics. The intended exact path costs are Conqueror [500,1100,2400,5200,13000], Observation [500,1000,2300,4800,12000], Armament [550,1200,2600,5600,13000]. These are numerical game prices from bounded encounter evidence, not new canon assertions. Return the entire valid unit, not a patch. Do not modify powers or descriptions to justify cost changes. Do not reintroduce primary-only contactStun prose.

candidateToRefine.name: Monkey D. Luffy
candidateToRefine.description: Straw Hat captain, manga through Wano; stationary long-range stretched contact, not ammunition. Numbers, prices, caps, unlocks and stamina are provisional tuning, not canon or measured balance. Highest path tier unlocks Second/Third/all Fourth/Fifth at 1/2/3/5. One replacement primary and contextual Technique button; none in base. Second's tier-2 Gigant Jet Shell replaces Jet Gatling: brief Second+Third, no simultaneous forms or travel. Fourth's authored power includes Haki; purchases specialize it, not canon prerequisites. Snakeman uses fast contacts and single-target Black Mamba; curved trajectories, acceleration and obstacle bypass omitted. Selectable Stuffed Tankman without feeding adapts repeatable recoil and commanded Cannonball: no incoming strikes, trapping or enemy-projectile collisions; Cannonball reports bounded displacement. Fifth's unnamed Wano hook slows eligible targets as bodily rubberization, not terrain or reality alteration. Bajrang Gun is capped, not island-scale; noncontact Haki uses direct geometry, penetration from purchases. Shared exhaustion/base recovery replace distinct Gear drawbacks, including Fourth's ten-minute Haki lockout; purchased Haki stays active in base. Purchased contactStun applies to every damaging direct attack, including Techniques; requires weakWilled and stunnable. Boss immunity requires stunnable=false or weakWilled=false; boss tag alone does not block it. Shared onHit immuneTo boss rules are separate. Omitted: defensive rubber, lightning immunity, poison resistance, shields, evasion, flight, traversal, food healing, Seastone interactions, Voice of All Things, borrowed Nightmare form, improvised equipment, lightning throwing and unselected moves. No post-Wano names. Caller supplies motion/injuries; no enemy following or defensive combat.

primary.name: Enlarged Spinning Hook — Unnamed Wano Attack

paths.name: Conqueror Haki
paths.description: Selective intimidation becomes bounded stuns, then Supreme King coating increases attack power. Purchased contactStun applies to every damaging direct attack, including Techniques. Contact and pulse stuns require both weakWilled and stunnable; existing stun and its following protection block reapplication. Boss immunity to these legacy stuns requires stunnable=false or weakWilled=false; a boss tag alone does not block them. Shared onHit immuneTo boss rules are separate and do not confer immunity to the legacy modifiers. Pulses deal no damage. This path alone owns pulse configuration. Sky splitting is not terrain or weather control.

upgrades.name: Focused Intimidation
upgrades.description: Every damaging direct attack, including Techniques, can stun for 0.4 seconds when both weakWilled and stunnable are true, subject to stun protection. Boss immunity requires stunnable=false or weakWilled=false, not a boss tag alone; shared onHit immuneTo boss rules are separate.

upgrades.name: Selective Supreme King Burst
upgrades.description: Every four successful primary cycles can trigger a radius-30 pulse stunning up to six eligible enemies for 1 second, at least 5 seconds apart.

upgrades.name: Fish-Man Island Resolve
upgrades.description: Replaces the pulse with radius 45, cap 12 and 1.5-second stun; requires three successful primary cycles and at least 4 seconds between pulses. A bounded interpretation, not 50,000 targets.

upgrades.name: Supreme King Infusion
upgrades.description: Multiplies primary and all Technique damage by 1.35; coating improves offense even against enemies immune to intimidation.

upgrades.name: Emperor's Coating
upgrades.description: Further multiplies primary and all Technique damage by 1.5. Raises contact stun on every damaging direct attack, including Techniques, to 0.8 seconds without overriding longer simultaneous pulse stuns. Requires both weakWilled and stunnable, subject to stun protection. Boss immunity requires stunnable=false or weakWilled=false, not a boss tag alone; shared onHit immuneTo boss rules are separate.

paths.name: Observation Haki
paths.description: Presence sensing detects concealment; improved attack placement extends effective reach, permits one primary replacement target and shortens primary timing. These are bounded offensive interpretations of Observation and future sight, not future-motion simulation, guaranteed hits, evasion or obstacle bypass. Techniques keep their locked target.

upgrades.name: Sense Presence
upgrades.description: Enables concealed-target detection for acquisition and eligible contacts; obstacles and invulnerability remain separate checks.

upgrades.name: Read Intent
upgrades.description: Adds 3 reach and allows one replacement for a lost primary target at resolution without restarting windup. Never retargets Techniques.

upgrades.name: Katakuri's Lesson
upgrades.description: Multiplies primary windup and cycle timing by 0.85. Technique timing is unchanged.

upgrades.name: Udon Foresight
upgrades.description: Adds another 5 effective reach and multiplies primary timing by another 0.9.

upgrades.name: Sustained Future Sight
upgrades.description: Multiplies primary timing by another 0.75, improving repeated contact cadence without accelerating Techniques or guaranteeing contact.

paths.name: Armament Haki
paths.description: Hardening adds offense and armor penetration; advanced emission and internal destruction supply bounded follow-through and armor-bypassing damage. This path alone owns emission configuration. Emission starts at primary contact, extends away from Luffy and stops at obstacles; it excludes flat damage additions and never advances counters. Logia tangibility, defensive hardening and explosive-cuff removal are omitted, not invulnerability bypasses.

upgrades.name: Armament Hardening
upgrades.description: Adds 4 damage to primary attacks and every hit of all Techniques before purchased multipliers.

upgrades.name: Reinforced Fists
upgrades.description: Ignores 25% of armor on ordinary primary and Technique damage.

upgrades.name: Hyougoro's Emission Lesson
upgrades.description: Adds 2 reach. Every three successful primary cycles emit a bounded 24-damage follow-through, width 6 and length 14, hitting up to three targets.

upgrades.name: Internal Destruction
upgrades.description: Converts 35% of primary and Technique damage into internal damage that bypasses armor, never invulnerability.

upgrades.name: Mastered Internal Flow
upgrades.description: Raises internal fraction to 60%. Replaces emission with 42 damage, width 8, length 20 and cap four, now every two successful primary cycles.

context.independentReview: Matched-budget64-build moving evidence: at5000 old Luffy boss1338.8 vs Zoro623 and control241.6 vs Robin118.7. Doubling prices projects dense6534 below Franky9374/Robin8381, boss574.4 below Zoro623, control64.4 below Robin118.7/Usopp76.7. Concealed6453 retains premium broad capability.1.5x pricing failed to remove boss/control dominance;2x selected. This is price-only projection of actual measured build policies, not new attack measurements.

knowledge.subject: Monkey D. Luffy
gaps: All six supplied captures were considered through their endings, including later ability sections, references, situational techniques and navigation. Each reports acquisitionTruncated=false. Only supplied text was available: linked manga chapters, images, supplementary publications and other technique pages were not independently inspected.

The evidence is chiefly fan-wiki prose or wikitext, supplemented by the ONE PIECE.com Wano summary. Embedded chapter references support temporal filtering but are not separately acquired sources or independent verification of every interpretation.

The continuity is explicitly requested, so no default-continuity assumption is needed. General character facts were resolved from the character-specific abilities page rather than from the navigation lists or an unprovided standalone biography.

Post-Wano material is excluded, including Egghead and Elbaph battles, hearing Emet, later Haki interactions with immortality, Domi Reversi immunity claims, isolated Mini Gear Four, and the manga Elephant Whip introduced in Chapter 1127. Later navigation entries do not expand the selected record.

Gear 5's later named repertoire is excluded: Mole Pistol, Dawn Whip, Dawn Rocket, Dawn Stamp, the named Star Gun execution, Dawn Gatling, Dawn Cymbal, Dawn Balloon, Dawn Pistol, Tummy Cracker, Gear 5 Jet Gatling, Genie, Caught-You-Slipping Bullet, Dawn Kraken Gatling, Dawn Thor Rifle and Dawn Thor Bullet. The Wano precursor associated retrospectively with Star Gun is retained only as an unnamed attack.

Adaptation-only and game-only techniques and variants are not merged into manga evidence. This includes the anime Jet Lance naming, Jet Missile, Jet Rifle and Jet Axe uses; later anime-only Hawk attacks; game Red Hawk upgrades, Eagle Storm and Gigant Jet Gatling; Giant Fly Swatter, Grizzly Corkscrew Magnum, film Thor attacks, One Piece Party situational moves, Leo Rex Bazooka, King King King Kong Gun, King Kong Gatling, Rhino Stampede, Dragon Culverin, Counterblow and licensed-game Gear 5 finishers.

The pages' broad descriptions of Gear 5 turning anything imagined into reality rely partly on their interpretation of Road To Laugh Tale. They also qualify object creation as uncertain and the power as non-omnipotent. This record retains demonstrated Wano rubberization, shape changes and cartoonish physical effects, not unrestricted reality alteration or permanent object creation.

Some summaries reverse the fruit-name chronology or retain Paramecia labels in navigation. The character page's explicit Wano revelation supports Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika as the true Mythical Zoan identity and Gomu Gomu no Mi as the previously used name.

Gear 2 lifespan loss is presented more categorically in some summary wording than in the detailed page's attribution to Lucci's speculation. No quantified Gear 2 lifespan loss is established. Similarly, later improvements do not justify erasing Gear 4's explicitly retained Onigashima time limit and Haki exhaustion.

The detailed Gear 4 page distinguishes the demonstrated Tankman: Stuffed Version from an unknown ordinary Tankman. The main page's generic Tankman summary cannot establish an additional observed unstuffed form.

The Gear 5 page supports cutting vulnerability and taxing use, but several detailed claims about aged appearance, recovery after deactivation, food-based immediate restoration and awakened Zoan personality takeover cite post-Wano chapters. Those later explanations are not backdated as established Wano facts.

The supplied pages do not give a systematic account of swimming inability or water-submersion thresholds. Their mention of balloon buoyancy and navigation links to the Blue Sea is insufficient to reconstruct those mechanics. No unsupported memory-based water rules are added.
The Thor Elephant Gun page calls its sparks lightning enhancement but does not establish a general ability to generate or control electricity. Its film-only Thor Axe comparison is excluded.

The main page's Nightmare Luffy skin-color reference appears internally malformed, and the supplied text mixes manga and anime color evidence. The core borrowed-shadow transformation is retained without depending on that color citation.

A complete baseline Gomu Gomu technique page was not supplied. Numerous original attacks are identified indirectly through Gear variants, but unsupported detailed descriptions of every baseline move are not reconstructed. No user guidance requested additional features, and allowUnverified=false prevents adding memory-based claims.

findings.message: Pulse and emission cycles count successful primary attack cycles required for one trigger, not waves per trigger. A cycle counts once when at least one primary hit applies positive damage, regardless of collateral targets. Pulses apply stun without damage; their event amount counts affected targets. Emissions apply their declared damage. Pulse intervals can further limit trigger frequency.

gaps: The candidate does not satisfy the user's exact price-only preservation requirement: its root description removes the supplied original's three sentences about purchased contactStun scope, dual eligibility, boss-tag handling and separate shared onHit rules. Those rules remain correctly described in the Conqueror path and upgrades, so this is a preservation failure rather than a changed executable stun mechanic.

All sixteen requested prices match the intended doubled values. Purchase value and the author's encounter-balance assessment are not established by character evidence and were not treated as canon evidence.
This is a bounded review of supplied passages, chiefly fan-wiki summaries and wikitext. Linked manga panels and supplementary publications were not independently inspected.

Several sources mix Wano material with later developments and adaptation-only details. Findings use the selected manga-era effects; later Star Gun naming, Kizaru-specific immobility, Mini Gear Four and unrestricted reality alteration were not imported.

The adaptation intentionally omits major defensive and movement traits and simplifies Tankman's reactive setup, Snakeman trajectories, literal bodily deformation and distinct Gear exhaustion consequences. The executable subset therefore represents selected offensive effects, not Luffy's complete combat capabilities.
